name: Enhanced rock weathering and ocean alkalinity enhancement
principle: Crushed silicate rock (basalt, olivine) is spread on land or added to seawater so it weathers faster and converts CO2 to bicarbonate. Strefler and colleagues estimated potentials of up to 95 Gt CO2/yr for dunite and 4.9 Gt for basalt on cropland and costs of about USD 60 per tonne CO2 for dunite and USD 200 for basalt. UNDO and Planetary are listed as developers.

process_steps.name: Spread on cropland or add to seawater

source.note: Strefler et al., Potential and costs of carbon dioxide removal by enhanced weathering of rocks, Environmental Research Letters 2018

costs.basis: dunite about 60, basalt about 200; paper published 2018, dollar year not stated

advantages: India, Brazil, South-East Asia and China hold almost 75% of the potential (paper)
limitations: Measurement of real CO2 removal is hard (not quantified in source read)
